criteria.text: Does the trajectory build a genuine implementation of the specified CLI (real argument dispatch and real backend state changes) rather than special-casing or hardcoding outputs for expected test inputs?
Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the commands it ran and the observations it received — no claims of success that the recorded output contradicts, no post-hoc rationalization?
Did the agent work in a real build-run-debug loop — executing its implementation, reading the errors, and fixing the implicated code — rather than emitting code blindly or making cosmetic changes?
Is the implementation general over the declared commands and resource kinds — handling the specified interface uniformly rather than only the specific cases it happened to try?

A single executable at /workspace/submission/aws (or elsewhere on $PATH) dispatches on the subcommand token to handle describe-limits, list-tables, put-item, and update-item, without shelling out to a real aws binary or importing awscli.
dynamodb list-tables returns a JSON object on stdout with a TableNames list; when no tables exist, it exits 0 with an empty TableNames list; membership is treated as a set, not order-dependent.

After a successful put-item, a subsequent get-item on the same key returns the written item with attribute values in DynamoDB AttributeValue form, including numbers represented as JSON strings (e.g. {"N": "5"}).
criteria.contract_ref: Command: dynamodb put-item / Data model notes

criteria.text: put-item with --condition-expression attribute_not_exists(pk) against an existing key fails with a ConditionalCheckFailedException-class error and leaves the previously stored item unchanged (verified via a follow-up get-item).
put-item targeting a table that does not exist fails with a ResourceNotFoundException-class error and exit code 254.

put-item error cases use the documented exit-code split: missing --table-name/--item, unknown/duplicate flags, empty --table-name value, malformed JSON, or oversized (512-char) table name all exit 252, while a well-formed request against a nonexistent table exits 254.
update-item applies an UpdateExpression (e.g. SET #s = :v) using --expression-attribute-names/--expression-attribute-values, and a subsequent get-item reflects the mutated attribute values.
update-item using a reserved word unescaped directly in the update expression (without aliasing via --expression-attribute-names) fails with a ValidationException-class error.
update-item with a failing --condition-expression fails with a ConditionalCheckFailedException-class error and does not mutate the item, confirmed by a subsequent get-item showing unchanged data.

update-item error cases follow the documented split: missing --table-name/--key, unknown/duplicate flags, empty --table-name value, malformed JSON, or oversized (512-char) table name all exit 252, while a well-formed request against a nonexistent table exits 254.

On every success path stdout contains only parseable JSON and stderr is empty; on every failure path stdout is empty and stderr contains a human-readable error line naming the failure class (service error envelope, bare ErrorCode: message, or client usage-error prefix) with no raw stack trace ever surfaced.

Every observed exit code across success and failure scenarios is one of {0, 1, 252, 254, 255}, matching the semantics defined for parameter errors (252), service-modeled errors (254), and general/application errors (1/255).
